title: fcVM buckling_U100_3D: elastic buckling factor
prompt:
Linear (eigenvalue) buckling analysis of a steel structure from the fcVM workbench examples (buckling_U100_3D). analysis.step holds the analysis geometry in millimetres (1 solid region(s) that share their interfaces and act as one continuous body, volume 1207500 mm^3). faces.json describes every face (index, type, area, centroid, normal/axis).
Material: linear isotropic elastic, E = 210000 MPa, Poisson ratio 0.3.
Supports: (1) all displacement components = 0 on face 11: plane, area 1207.50 mm^2, centroid (19.502, 0.0, 0.0) mm, outward normal (-0.0, -0.0, -1.0).
Reference load set (load factor 1): (1) uniform traction (-0.0, -0.0, -41.407867) MPa on face 10: plane, area 1207.50 mm^2, centroid (19.502, 0.0, 1000.0) mm, outward normal (0.0, 0.0, 1.0). (2) uniform traction (1.656315, 0.0, 0.0) MPa on face 10: plane, area 1207.50 mm^2, centroid (19.502, 0.0, 1000.0) mm, outward normal (0.0, 0.0, 1.0). Self-weight is part of the reference load: density 7900 kg/m^3, gravity (0.0, 0.0, -10.0) m/s^2 (body force (0.0, 0.0, -7.9e-05) N/mm^3).
Analysis: compute the linear prebuckling stress state under the reference load set, then the elastic buckling load factors lambda (eigenvalues of K + lambda K_G = 0, the whole reference load set scaled by lambda). Report the smallest positive one.

Outputs:
- lambda1 [-]: first (smallest positive) elastic buckling load factor of the reference load set

Submit results.json containing exactly an outputs object with these numeric keys. Also submit main.py, part.step, mesh.msh, fields.npz, solver.log, refinement.json and environment.json. See candidate README for the artifact contract. Correct numerical answers alone do not establish workflow completion.

outputs.definition: first (smallest positive) elastic buckling load factor of the reference load set
